correctness.rationale: A 1-limited set is encoded by white bits in two-vertex twisted columns; each vertex condition becomes c_{i-1,r}+c_{i+1,r}+c_{i,1-r}<=1+c_{i,r}. The 16-state ordered-column transfer with twist J correctly counts each labeled configuration once. The signed trace splits into 7-dimensional symmetric and 3-dimensional antisymmetric cyclic cores; exact independent symbolic determinants equal (1-tz)(1-Q(t,z)) and 1-tz+t²z. Formal -t partial_t log(det) yields all F_n, and deficit a-b of Q monomials gives the sharp degree and multiplicities. The n=1,2 series coefficients are auxiliary, not claims for simple cubic graphs. The example F3=1+6z+9z², F4=1+8z+12z²+8z³+4z⁴ checks complement weighting. Brute enumeration of all subsets for n=3..8 matches the transfer profiles; no infinite result is claimed from finite checks.
residual_risks: Proof relies on correct restriction of twisted 16-state transfer to specified cyclic-core bases; determinant checks and finite comparisons provide independent corroboration.
No claim for n<3 or unlabeled quotient; finite brute enumeration is not all-n proof.

Relevant 2026 1-limited-domination papers study Cartesian products and Goldberg snarks; an OEIS/Möbius-ladder minimal dominating-set count concerns inclusion-minimal ordinary domination, a distinct predicate. Resultary semantic search returned domination polynomial results for chain and multipartite graphs, not this Möbius ladder predicate. This supports qualified best-of-knowledge originality, not absence of unindexed older enumerators.
residual_risks: Unindexed 1-limited dominating-set transfer enumerators could be equivalent; keyword/semantic search alone is not a novelty proof.

value.rationale: The exact generating function simultaneously counts every feasible size of 1-limited dominating sets on a natural, widely used cubic graph family. It refines a previously known extremal domination number and supplies previously uncatalogued optimum multiplicities in two other residue classes. Such enumerators are natural complete invariants and reusable for asymptotic or probabilistic combinatorics; the result is not merely recomputing a small finite table.
residual_risks: No broader combinatorial consequences or asymptotics established; intrinsic all-size classification suffices for the stated value.

limitations: Simple labeled Möbius ladders only, n>=3; z measures white/excluded vertices.
